note: Attacker-controlled Markdown text, containing embedded NUL (0x00) and control bytes, is handed to the parser with its full size.
The raw input (including NUL bytes) is stored in ctx->text; all ctx->size bytes are processed.
The document is split into lines; lines containing NUL bytes are analyzed as ATX-header/text lines.
Lines beginning with '#' (e.g. '# h1', '#### h4', '#*#####\0') are recognized as ATX headers.
Inline mark collection runs over each line, including lines whose contents contain NUL characters and emphasis characters.

code: if(ch == _T('\0')) { PUSH_MARK(ch, off, off+1, MD_MARK_RESOLVED); off++; continue; }
note: NUL bytes are materialized as resolved marks in ctx->marks; the mark-chain and emphasis resolution logic assumes a NUL-free mark stream, so the broken state corrupts mark indices/links used later.
Inline rendering walks the (now corrupted) mark vector and emits text slices of ctx->text; an out-of-bounds mark->beg/end causes an out-of-bounds read/write in the renderer.
